scope: Proposition 4.1 (Short root labels) of the manuscript “Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy” (preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/etr-counting-hierarchy.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 141 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 151fe6144a42154d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let P(t) and b0(t) be controlled families of integer univariate polynomials, indexed by the same input word. There is a uniformly controlled family La(t) ∈ Z[t], with labels a of polynomial binary length in a polynomial-time specified range, such that whenever P ̸= 0: (i) For every label a and every real root α of P, either La(α) ≥ 1 2 or La(α) ≤ −1 2. (ii) For every label a and every real root α of P, if La(α) > 0, then b0(α) > 0. (iii) For every real root α of P with b0(α) > 0, some label a satisfies La(α) > 0 and La(β) < 0 at every distinct real root β of P. The construction is defined and controlled also when P = 0, but no root-selection property is asserted in that case. It uses a fixed number of applications of the controlled-family rules, independent of the degrees. Taking b0 = 1 permits every real root to be selected.
